correctness.rationale: The reciprocal equals a fixed center plus a Gaussian projection ratio: a normal variable divided by an independent chi-square norm. This gives an exact Student-t distribution and an everywhere-positive smooth density. Local density at zero gives each one-sided Pareto coefficient, the exact moment range, and the logarithmic truncated mean. Symmetric/antisymmetric characteristic-function decomposition gives a rigorous Cauchy-domain limit with location the convergent principal-value integral and scale πf_R(0). The eigenvector boundary is deterministic. A standalone script passed 1,562 finite algebraic, distributional and limit-law checks; the written proof, not simulation, supports the quantified theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a reliability issue for a specified randomized harmonic extraction step: expected magnitude and naive replication averaging are invalid even for SPD matrices and any arbitrarily large finite Gaussian sketch width. Its exact t^{-1} tail coefficient and nondegenerate Cauchy averaging law quantify why rare, unstable denominators invalidate first-moment performance metrics; the ordinary sketched Rayleigh--Ritz comparison isolates the inversion mechanism. It is not an arbitrary chosen invariant or a textbook restatement of a generic probability law; application to a newly analyzed numerical projection and the exact stable limit are mathematically motivated by the source method.
